2.5.1.5-r1.burton_quote: fortify and strengthen the heart and brain, which are commonly both affected in this malady, and do mutually misaffect one another

2.5.1.5-r11.burton_quote: and Bezoar-stone hath an especial virtue against all melancholy affections, it refresheth the heart, and corroborates the whole body

2.5.1.5-r12.burton_quote: Amber provokes urine, helps the stomach, breaks wind, &c.

2.5.1.5-r13.burton_quote: suspects Alkermes, by reason of its heat, nothing (saith he) sooner exasperates this disease, than the use of hot-working meats and medicines, and would have them for that cause warily taken

2.5.1.5-r14.translation: For alienation of mind and foolishness arising from a fault of the brain, I found such a medicine in a German manuscript book.

2.5.1.5-r15.burton_quote: Ram’s head that never meddled with an Ewe, cut off at a blow, and the horns only taken away, boil it well skin and wool together, after it is well sod, take out the brains, and put these spices to it

2.5.1.5-r16.burton_quote: of the flowers of water lilies, Lettuce, Violets, Camomile, wild Mallows, wether’s head, &c.

2.5.1.5-r17.burton_quote: repeats many medicines which he tried, but two alone which did the cure; use of whey made of Goat’s milk, with the extract of Hellebore, and irrigations of the head with water lilies, lettuce, violets, camomile, &c., upon the suture of the crown
2.5.1.5-r17.translation: by these remedies he recovered his former health.

2.5.1.5-r18.burton_quote: Piso commends a Ram’s lungs applied hot to the fore-part of the head, or a young Lamb divided in the back, exenterated

2.5.1.5-r19.burton_quote: the seeds of Cumin, Rue, Carrots, Dill, have been boiled

2.5.1.5-r2.burton_quote: it makes those which are otherwise dull, to exhale & evaporate like frankincense

2.5.1.5-r3.burton_quote: or quicken (Xenophon adds) as oil doth fire

2.5.1.5-r4.burton_quote: A famous Cordial Matthiolus in Dioscoridem calls it, an excellent nutriment to refresh the body, it makes a good colour, a flourishing age, helps concoction, fortifies the stomach, takes away obstructions, provokes urine, drives out excrements, procures sleep, clears the blood, expels wind and cold poisons, attenuates, concocts, dissipates all thick vapours, and fuliginous humours
2.5.1.5-r4.translation: for preserving strength; it cherishes the innate heat

2.5.1.5-r5.burton_quote: spent his time with dice and drink that he might so ease his discontented mind, and avoid those continual cogitations of his present condition wherewith he was tormented

2.5.1.5-r6.burton_quote: because it scours the body by vomit, urine, sweat, of all manner of superfluities, and keeps it clean

2.5.1.5-r8.burton_quote: so that the liver be not incensed

2.5.1.5-r9.burton_quote: for 24 hours following, takes away all sense of grief, makes them incline to laughter and mirth
